notes: Inbound via self-serve sign-up; promo email triggered demo request 2026-03-02.
Use-case: chat-based customer support for e-commerce merchants (multitenant). Main flow: end-user -> Emberly -> Redwood hosted API -> response returned to merchant channels.
Experiencing 429s during morning peak (10:00-11:30 PT): ~5% of requests get 429s; intermittent spikes after marketing pushes.
They have moderate cost sensitivity; want to keep 'tokens per dollar' high. Prefer hosted API first, may consider Dedicated later if predictable throughput needed.
Concurrency: typical concurrent chats 60-120 sessions during peaks; reported bursts up to 350 concurrent connections for special events.
Targets: p95 latency <300ms for generation start; durable throughput ~200 requests/minute sustained; spike handling to 600r/min for 5-10m.
Wants clear per-org & per-api-key quotas, burst buckets, and documented 'Retry-After' behavior. Also SDK-level backoff and idempotency for avoiding double completions.
Security: SOC2 ok, requires audit logs and token rotation; no VPC/on-prem needs.
Quote from CTO: 'We can't afford silent 429s during Black Friday-style campaigns — need graceful degradation and surge credits or predictable burst buffer.'
Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching, caching) to lower cost for embeddings used in context retrieval.
